title: Callgraph Pathfinder — interactive execution map for request correlation
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Engineers using the Console need a low-friction way to understand how a single user request traverses services and kernels in the Redwood serving runtime. Existing list-and-waterfall views surface spans, but teams report difficulty locating causal edges, quickly comparing latency contributors, and following correlation IDs across retries and cached responses.

Goal: Prototype an interactive 'Callgraph Pathfinder' — a compact, time-synced execution map that complements the timeline and span list. The Pathfinder emphasizes causal edges (calls/requests), latency sparkline overlays, and quick correlation ID tracing across retries and fallbacks. It should be usable as a focused drill-down panel within the Request Inspector and as a detachable workspace for longer investigations.

Key concepts in this prototype: compact node-edge callgraph (service + operation nodes), edge-bundled path highlighting for the active request, per-edge latency sparklines, span detail flyout, correlation ID breadcrumbs, time-range scrubber linked to the main timeline, and multi-filter support (service, status, kernel type, cache-hit). The prototype explores a hybrid of edge-centric and timeline-centric navigation to reduce context switching.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates an interactive callgraph view embedded in the Request Inspector with nodes representing services and operations
Selecting a node or edge highlights the associated spans in the timeline and in the span list (time-synced selection)
Edge hover reveals a latency sparkline and summary metrics (p50/p95/failed_count) in a tooltip
Correlation ID breadcrumb shows the propagation path across retries and cached responses, with a one-click copy and deep-link action
Filters allow narrowing to service, status code class, kernel/adapter type, and cache-hit flag; filters update graph and timeline in real time
Prototype includes accessible keyboard navigation for node selection and tooltips
Design handoff assets (Figma frames + spec) uploaded and linked; PM/ENG sign-off on UX patterns
comments: 2026-03-01 - Ava Chen: Kickoff notes — consolidated user interviews (Ops + Platform teams) report that debugging multi-hop requests is the top friction for SLO investigations. Decided to prioritize a lightweight, embeddable visualization rather than a full graph explorer to minimize scope.

2026-03-03 - Julian Ortega: Initial wireframes added to Figma. Chose edge-bundling to reduce visual clutter for common call fan-outs. Prototype will only show up to 50 nodes in the quick view; a detachable large-view will stream more if needed.

2026-03-04 - PM (Ravi Singh): PM feedback — ensure graph respects time-sliced spans (we cannot aggregate spans outside the selected request window). Also call out privacy constraints when visualizing cached payload identifiers — use hashes only.

2026-03-05 - ENG (Maya Torres): Engineering feasibility notes — building the graph will require a new backend endpoint that returns pre-joined call edges for a request trace. ENG will add an API task (ENG-49012) and follow up with data contract. KV cache hits are available but need standardized flagging in the trace model.

2026-03-07 - Design review: UX critiques — reduce reliance on color saturation for status (add shape/label), increase contrast for small sparklines, and add affordance for 'show related correlation IDs' in the flyout. Action: update prototype and add keyboard focus states.

2026-03-08 - Accessibility review (Carlos Kim): Suggest larger hit targets for nodes and an ARIA live region for tooltip summaries when focus changes. Also request that copy/deep-link actions have descriptive labels for screen readers.

2026-03-09 - Julian Ortega: Updated prototype uploaded to Figma with revised color tokens, keyboard nav, and an example deep-link query string pattern (console?request_id=...&focus=edge-7). Added notes on performance trade-offs for real-time updates versus snapshot refresh.

2026-03-10 - Ava Chen: Design ready for PM/ENG sync. Follow-ups: ENG to estimate backend endpoint and streaming costs (ENG-49012), PM to decide retention policy for callgraph-computed edges (PM-2201), and Design to prepare final handoff file and spec annotations for console-2026.03 release.

2026-03-10 - QA note: Plan a short usability study with 6 engineers (ops + platform) to validate that the Pathfinder reduces mean time to root cause on a set of 8 canonical incidents. Recording session and metrics framework linked in Confluence.
